framework.name: Brennan & Resnick (2012) computational thinking dimensions, with CT Quest sub-nodes
framework.decision: Chosen by Akmal on 2026-09-26. See docs/adr/0001-ct-platform-model.md.

primary.citation: Brennan, K. & Resnick, M. (2012). New frameworks for studying and assessing the development of computational thinking. Paper presented at the annual meeting of the American Educational Research Association, Vancouver, Canada.

extensions.note: Sub-nodes added beneath the Brennan & Resnick nodes where CT Quest questions need finer grain. The top two levels are Brennan & Resnick only.

bebrasCategory.citation: Dagiene, V., Sentance, S. & Stupuriene, G. (2017). Developing a two-dimensional categorization system for educational tasks in informatics. Informatica 28(1). Informatics domains axis.

bebrasSkill.citation: Same categorisation, computational thinking skills axis.

nodes.label: Computational concepts
nodes.description: Ideas that programs and algorithms are built from.

nodes.label: Sequences
nodes.description: Steps carried out in a particular order, where order matters.

nodes.label: Loops
nodes.description: Running the same steps several times, a fixed number of times or until a condition holds.

nodes.label: Events
nodes.description: One thing causing another to happen, such as a button press triggering code.

nodes.label: Parallelism
nodes.description: Sequences of steps happening at the same time.

nodes.label: Conditionals
nodes.description: Choosing what to do based on whether a condition is true.

nodes.label: Operators
nodes.description: Mathematical, logical and string operations on values.

nodes.label: Logic operators
nodes.description: Combining conditions with AND, OR and NOT, and reasoning about which rule takes priority.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.description: Storing, retrieving and updating values.

nodes.label: Variables and state
nodes.description: Named values that change as a program or process runs.

nodes.label: Data representation
nodes.description: Encoding information so a computer can store and process it.

nodes.label: Binary and counting states
nodes.description: Bits, how many states n bits can hold, and how many bits data needs.

nodes.label: Text and strings
nodes.description: Sequences of characters, pattern matching and simple text transformations.

nodes.label: Encryption
nodes.description: Transforming a message so only someone who knows the rule can read it.

nodes.label: Data structures
nodes.description: Lists, grids and graphs that organise data so it can be processed.

nodes.label: Paths and routing
nodes.description: Shortest, cheapest and counted routes through grids and graphs.

nodes.label: Searching and sorting
nodes.description: Finding and ordering items in a collection, and comparing how much work each strategy needs in the worst case.

nodes.label: Computational practices
nodes.description: Ways of working while solving problems computationally.

nodes.label: Experimenting and iterating
nodes.description: Building a little, trying it, and improving it in cycles.

sources.term: being incremental and iterative (experimenting and iterating)

nodes.label: Testing and debugging
nodes.description: Making sure things work, and finding and fixing the cause when they do not.

nodes.label: Tracing and predicting
nodes.description: Stepping through a procedure or program by hand to predict exactly what it does.

sources.term: finer grain under testing and debugging

nodes.label: Choosing edge cases
nodes.description: Picking inputs, such as equal values or negative numbers, that expose mistakes.

sources.term: finer grain under testing and debugging

nodes.label: Reviewing AI-generated code
nodes.description: Reading code an AI assistant produced, predicting its behaviour and finding inputs where it fails.

nodes.label: Reusing and remixing
nodes.description: Making something by building on existing projects, code or ideas.

nodes.label: Translating between languages
nodes.description: Recognising the same algorithm written in different programming languages, such as Swift and Python.

sources.term: finer grain under reusing and remixing

nodes.label: Building with AI assistants
nodes.description: Directing an AI assistant to produce code (vibe coding) and building on what it gives back.

nodes.label: Abstracting and modularizing
nodes.description: Exploring connections between the whole and the parts; keeping the details that matter.

nodes.label: Decomposition
nodes.description: Breaking a problem into smaller parts that can be solved separately.

sources.term: finer grain under abstracting and modularizing

nodes.label: Pattern recognition and generalisation
nodes.description: Spotting a repeating structure and using it to predict or to solve related problems.

sources.term: finer grain under abstracting and modularizing

nodes.label: Finding invariants
nodes.description: Noticing a property that every allowed move preserves and using it to rule states out.

sources.term: finer grain under abstracting and modularizing

nodes.label: Computational perspectives
nodes.description: How learners see themselves, others and the world in relation to computing.

nodes.label: Expressing
nodes.description: Seeing computation as a way to create and express ideas.

nodes.label: Connecting
nodes.description: Creating with and for other people.

nodes.label: Questioning
nodes.description: Asking questions about technology and how it works.

nodes.label: Questioning AI output
nodes.description: Treating what an AI assistant produces as a claim to check rather than an answer to trust.
